newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AMBROSE RIPS THROUGH AUSTRALIA AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AMBROSE RIPS THROUGH AUSTRALIA AGAIN.

text.p: West Indies fast-bowler Curtly Ambrose sent Australia tumbling towards almost certain defeat after a second innings collapse in the third test on Saturday.
Ambrose, who took five for 55 in the first innings, added four more wickets to his match tally as Australia sank to 122 all out at tea on the third day at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
West Indies need to score 87 runs to win the test, cutting Australia's lead to 2-1 in the five-test series.
Fellow pace-bowler and West Indies captain Courtney Walsh and Kenneth Benjamin took three wickets each as the tourists ripped through the batting order.
West Indies were dismissed for 255 in the first hour of play during which they added 22 runs to their overnight first innings total for the loss of their last wicket.
Left-hander Jimmy Adams, batting at number six, remained unbeaten on 74, the highest score of the match to date.
Australia lost captain Mark Taylor, opener Matthew Hayden and number three Justin Langer before overhauling the 36-run deficit.

All-rounder Steve Waugh saved his side from even greater humiliation with a defiant 37 but he became the last wicket to fall when his middle stump was flattened by a full-length delivery from Benjamin.

Ambrose accounted for Hayden and Langer for ducks in his first three overs before returning late in the innings to dismiss bowlers Shane Warne and Jason Gillespie, despite the handicap of a slight calf strain.
